repo_files.title: NPPC Launches the NPPC Quiz, an Interactive Look at Political Repression in America
repo_files.why: A 2x2 composite built from four of the quizs own portrait cards, served from this site at /images/civic-profile/pp-01, pp-05, pp-07 and pp-10. NPPCs own artwork, recomposed; nothing new licensed, and it shows the reader what the quiz actually is.

measurement_note: Measured, not estimated. All 116 published articles were pulled from /news and every card image was requested: 85 resolve, 22 return 404, and 9 articles carry no image at all -- 31 needing a photograph. The 404s fall into two groups. Seventeen point at images/site/default-article.jpg, a placeholder path that does not exist on the server, so those articles were never given a photograph and the fallback was never created either. Five point at real storage/articles ULID uploads whose files are missing from disk.
not_a_restoration_note: The originals were checked before anything was substituted. Of the seventeen press releases republished from cldc.org, fifteen have no photograph on cldc.org either -- their own posts carry no featured image. So for most of these there is nothing to restore; a photograph has to be sourced from somewhere new. That is a different job from fixing a broken link, and it is why this batch stops where it does.
sourcing_rule: Every image here comes from something this archive already owns or hosts: its own prisoner portraits, its own product photography, its own quiz artwork. No third-party news photography was copied. That rule is what limits this batch to seven articles, and the twenty-four left are listed below rather than filled with whatever could be found.
wilansky_note: One image was found and deliberately not used. The CLDC post behind NORTH DAKOTA COURT RULING DISMISSES THE CIVIL RIGHTS CASE carries two court-exhibit photographs of Sophia Wilanskys arm after it was destroyed at Standing Rock. They are medical-evidence photographs of an open traumatic wound. Putting one into the /news thumbnail grid, where it would appear unannounced next to everything else, is an editorial decision for the curator and not one to make quietly inside a batch. The file is left alone.

remaining.decision_needed: These have no photograph in the archive and none on the original either. There are three honest options and they are the curators call: (a) the CLDC wordmark on the fifteen CLDC press releases -- the issuing organisations own mark on its own release, which is standard practice, carries no licensing risk, and identifies the source at a glance, but is a logo rather than a photograph; (b) public-domain and Creative-Commons substitutes -- Library of Congress, federal government works, Wikimedia Commons -- which are photographs and are safe to publish, but are illustrative rather than of the actual event; (c) licensed news photography, which is what most of these stories actually depict and which costs money or needs permission from the outlets cited on each article.
remaining.easy_wins_if_option_b_is_chosen: Four of the nine NPPC originals have obvious public-domain answers: the Espionage Act piece (1917-era Library of Congress material, or a Debs portrait), Political Trials and Prisoners (a federal courthouse), Johanna Fernandez (a Creative-Commons portrait, if one exists that is genuinely her), and the mobile-app release (a screenshot of the database the app carries). Mohammad Yousef Hasna is in this archive as a prisoner but has no photograph on his record either.
